valid_fixes: Restore the dynamodb:PutItem statement's Resource to !GetAtt InventoryUpdatesTable.Arn in InventoryFunctionRole inline policy
invalid_patches: Granting dynamodb:PutItem on a wildcard resource (*) — over-permissive and does not restore least-privilege scoping
Creating a new DynamoDB table named inventory-archive to match the policy ARN instead of correcting the policy resource
optimal_diagnostic_path: ace_describe_resource(resource=InventoryUpdatesTable) → table is ACTIVE with correct name — eliminates resource-not-found as cause
ace_get_iam_role(role=InventoryFunctionRole) → dynamodb:PutItem Resource ends in inventory-archive, not inventory-updates
ace_simulate_policy(action=dynamodb:PutItem, resource=InventoryUpdatesTable.Arn) → implicitDeny confirms mismatch between policy scope and actual table ARN
observable_symptom: CSV upload succeeds. Messages reach the work queue and the consumer function is invoked. Every consumer invocation fails with an access denied error on database writes. Messages exhaust retries and route to the dead-letter queue. No inventory records are persisted.
root_cause: The IAM role's dynamodb:PutItem policy statement scopes its Resource to a table named inventory-archive, but the consumer writes to the deployed table named inventory-updates. Every PutItem call is denied with AccessDeniedException despite the role appearing to have write permission.
